title: PostgreSQL JSONB: Operators, jsonb_path_query, and GIN Indexing
realWorldScenario: Your e-commerce product catalog stores dynamic technical specifications in a `specifications JSONB` column. Queries searching for products with `"ram_gb" >= 16` and `"color" IN ("space_gray", "silver")` are performing full table scans.
questionStatement: Compare JSON vs JSONB in PostgreSQL. Explain the core operators (`->`, `->>`, `@>`, `?`, `@@`). Write a query using PostgreSQL SQL/JSON path syntax (`jsonb_path_query` or `jsonb_path_match`) and specify the exact GIN index required to index deep key-value lookups efficiently.
expectedConcepts: JSON (text) vs JSONB (decomposed binary) storage format
Expression B-tree index vs GIN jsonb_path_ops index
hints: Which operator returns text versus JSONB?
Can a GIN index accelerate numeric range comparisons like ram_gb >= 16 out of the box?
Consider an expression B-Tree index for scalar casts.
